step1_analysis.description: A lumped-element pi-model representing an integrated spiral inductor. It models the main inductance (L1), series resistance (R3), feedforward capacitance (C3), and substrate parasitics including oxide capacitance (C1, C2) and substrate resistance (R1, R2).

paper_reference.title: Concepts and Methods in Optimization of Integrated LC VCOs

L_eff.description: Effective inductance at the operating frequency (2.4 GHz)

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined primarily by the L1 parameter in the pi-model, slightly modified by parasitic capacitances at 2.4 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper explicitly targets a 2.7 nH inductor for the 2.4 GHz VCO design.

Q_factor.description: Quality factor of the inductor at 2.4 GHz

sky130_expected.calculation: Q = Im(Z) / Re(Z) at 2.4 GHz. With L=2.7nH and Rs=2.5 ohms, Q ~ wL/Rs = (2*pi*2.4G*2.7n)/2.5 ~ 16.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical integrated spiral inductors in CMOS processes have Q factors in the range of 10 to 20 at low GHz frequencies.

SRF.description: Self-resonant frequency where the inductor's reactance crosses zero and becomes capacitive

sky130_expected.calculation: SRF = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C_total)). With L=2.7nH and C_total~150fF, SRF ~ 7.9 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The SRF must be significantly higher than the operating frequency (2.4 GHz) for the inductor to behave inductively and maintain a good Q factor.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the effective inductance, quality factor, and self-resonant frequency of the inductor pi-model.
